outs: R2172: repairing drifted evidence files was one manual path at a time and left no reproducible batch line. The new face censuses a whole directory, decodes every candidate before writing, repairs only the flagged .log files and rolls the batch back byte for byte on any failure, reporting before/after bytes and lines.

R2171: every price face answered a snapshot cross-section, so the seller's own high-frequency action - repricing - had no time-axis reading. The new face derives step percentages from two stored prices only and reports pooled mean, median, absolute peak and a signed sum against a market benchmark under a seller scope; a listing with live stock but no revision stays honestly absent.

R2170: repeat purchases counted events, the sales board totalled money and the buyer mirror face let only the buyer look - so a seller could not tell how many residents its net revenue hangs on or how much rides on the biggest one. The new face derives the roll from purchases x refunds (a fully refunded buyer stays at zero weight), reports share, top1/top3, a herfindahl computed from exact fractions and a pareto buyer count decided on integers, and carries the market-wide herfindahl as a comparable benchmark under a seller scope.

R2169: event rows, one trade end to end, the cash month and the repricing history existed, but nothing answered how long a shelf sat before it sold - so a high price, a bad description and a dead category were indistinguishable. The new face measures from the cycle opening (latest re-listing at or before the first NET sale, else the published stamp), reports an honestly unsold shelf that never drags the mean to zero, and carries a MARKET-scoped category benchmark that stays comparable under a seller scope.

R2167: the buyer profile answered only lifetime refunded amount and count, the refund register listed rows and the refund exposure was seller-side, so a resident with one refund out of three purchases and one with one out of thirty read the same and there was no market benchmark. The new face returns a sixteen-key envelope: purchase/refund counts over the whole purchase base, gross/refunded/net tokens, the count rate refund/purchase and the separate amount rate refunded/gross (both None rather than a fake zero), the market counts and count rate, the raw-minus-market delta, and the smoothed rate (refund + K*market)/(purchase + K) with K=10 whose deviation from the market is exactly the raw deviation scaled by n/(n+K) - on the fixture market rate 10/45 the one-purchase resident reads 1.0 raw but 0.2929 smoothed against the twenty-purchase resident 0.4 raw and 0.3407 smoothed, so a small sample stops being the scariest reading. Refund authority is the append-only refunds table so a new refund moves this face and the buyer profile together, delist/relist move nothing, the account gate is prefix-only before any read, and the face is a pure read with frozen table digests and a constant ledger_tx set.

R2164: api_buyer_profile answered only rating_count and an average, so whether a resident is consistently harsh or generous, whether it is stricter than the market, and how its stars spread had no face - the first judgement of rating credibility and of suspected score-padding. api_buyer_rating_pattern(buyer_id) returns a twenty-key aggregate envelope with the five-bucket star_distribution: distribution conservation both ways, star_sum from the buckets, avg/min/max honest None on an empty history, harsh (<=2), neutral (3) and generous (>=4) with their ratios, purchase coverage over every purchase including refunded ones, and a market-relative tendency_delta (negative = harsher than the market). Every star reads through the effective-stars seam, so a revision moves the whole envelope in one step while the base stamp is never rewritten and the revision counters keep the history; delisting, relisting and refunds never remove a rating. Run origin of the design: the R2149 reseed row, claimed with AC-BRP1..AC-BRP8 registered before the code. Suite 8/8 double-run byte-identical sha16 4e86f6f72ea4ac12, wired ledger-apimarket-buyerratingpattern(8); five adjacent suites green; full battery 366/366 plus controls 7/7 in 834.2s; matrix regenerated to 366 suites / 3050 criteria and --check byte-identical.

R2162: the listing-demand face gave per-listing watcher and converted COUNTS with no rate, no time-to-convert, no market-level or seller-level roll-up - and worse, its conversion test only asked whether the buyer ever holds a non-refunded purchase, never whether it came after the watch, so every buy-then-watch record was counted as converted and the funnel was permanently fake. api_watch_conversion(dev_account=None, include_uncategorized=True) returns a fifteen-key envelope with twelve-key category rows and fixes the direction: a live watch converts only when the non-refunded purchase stamp is at or after the watch stamp (same-second counts as a zero-second conversion), an earlier purchase is reported as pre_owned outside the funnel denominator, a refund returns the watch to pending, and watch_count equals pre_owned plus funnel while funnel equals converted plus pending. Durations are derived only from two stored stamps (integers, non-negative by construction, never the wall clock), the average is pooled rather than a mean of means, and the median takes the middle value for odd counts and the midpoint for even ones. Rows are watch-side with ascending categories and the uncategorized bucket last, the six counts conserve, and both the conversion rate and the pooled average are pinned as non-additive. Suite 8/8 double-run byte-identical criterion lines sha16 cc3abcdc8af89c87, wired ledger-apimarket-watchconversion(8); four adjacent suites green.

R2161: the library gives rows, the buyer profile lifetime aggregates, the seller profile gross totals and the category demand face volumes - none of them answered whether the same resident comes back, which is the most direct read of repeat business there is. api_repeat_purchase(dev_account=None) returns a twelve-key envelope with eight-key category rows. The counting authority is NET purchases: a refunded purchase enters neither the numerator nor the denominator, so a buyer whose only purchase was refunded disappears instead of being misread as a one-time buyer. repeat_purchase_count is purchase_count minus buyer_count, repeat_rate is None with zero buyers, and the extremes carry an account-name tie-break. The scopes differ honestly and the suite pins it: one purchase from each of two sellers is a repeat for the market and not a repeat for either seller. Category rows ride the one effective-bucket seam with purchase-side authority, and the additive law is pinned in two halves - purchase counts add up to the envelope while repeat counts do not, because a cross-bucket repeat is invisible inside each bucket. Suite 8/8 double-run byte-identical sha16 04fa0a8015207f95, wired ledger-apimarket-repeatpurchase(8); three adjacent buyer-family suites green.

R2159: the claim chain grew one door per round (open R2129, respond R2130, withdraw R2131, note R2137) and the question/answer pair already scored its waiting time, but the claim chain never produced a latency figure at all - api_seller_todo lists only unanswered rows, api_claims only status columns, api_claim_thread one thread, so whether a seller answers within a day or sits on claims had no answer. api_claim_latency(dev_account=None) reports a twelve-key envelope with sixteen-key rows: every leg of every claim folded into whole seconds measured from that claim own opened_utc (response, note, withdraw, refund), derived from two stored stamps only and never a wall clock, a leg that never happened being None rather than zero so an unanswered claim cannot look fast, and no negative duration possible because every action row references a claim that already exists. Status follows the api_claims seam so a later refund adds refund_seconds without rewriting the response leg, and the aggregate family (partition, coverage, average, median with odd middle and even midpoint, fastest, slowest, latest stamp) is all None on a world where nothing was answered. The usr: prefix gate runs before any read, the default is the operator market-wide view, and seller isolation is strict. Suite 8/8 double-run sha16 21df699d4434bdff, wired ledger-apimarket-claimlatency(8). Same window rejected the FIFO head before it: the seed claimed the reputation surface answered only means and counts, but api_seller_quality (R2117) already ships a seller-level five-bucket histogram, so the seed was a misreading of a live face and was marked negative with evidence instead of implemented.

R2158: the category axis answered where the money went, but inside one category the seller composition stayed unanswered - how many sellers this resident actually paid, which one took the largest share, and whether the resident is bound to a single counterparty. api_buyer_seller_spend derives it from purchases joined to listings with no new table: purchase-side row authority (a seller with live stock this buyer never bought from stays absent), a total order (-net_spent, -gross_spent, dev_account) so rank is a position and never a dense rank, four per-row conservation laws plus envelope sums, six cash figures identical to api_buyer_category_spend, net_share = net_spent / total with every row None when the total is not positive, refunds lowering only the net side while purchase/listing/seller survive, category_count riding the one effective-category seam, a seven-form account gate before any read and cross-restart byte identity.
